title: Game of the Week: Kapaun Mt. Carmel Crusaders vs. Bishop Carroll Golden Eagles - NewsBreak
text:
By Michael Emami Carina Branson ,
1 hours ago WICHITA, Kan. (KSNW) – This week’s Game of the Week isn’t just any game; this is the Holy War. Kapaun Mt. Carmel and Bishop Carroll, two Wichita-area Catholic schools with rich histories, will meet again on Friday.
Bishop Carroll, the long-time king of the rivalry, saw its 26-game win streak snapped just two seasons ago. Now, Kapaun is looking to build on its back-to-back wins.
For 24 years, Bishop Carroll was king until Kapaun finally took the crown two seasons ago, and since then, the Crusaders have started a streak of their own. Boasting a 5-0 start and back-to-back big wins against their cross-town rival, Kapaun’s confidence is unwavering.
“We’re feeling pretty good. We got a lot of momentum, and we just hope to keep that going forward. And we practiced the same way every week and take it one game at a time,” Kapaun senior cornerback Owen Young said.
Moving forward and up in the standings. Kapaun stunned Wichita Northwest in overtime just two weeks ago, and then just seven days later, put up 49 points to Wichita Southeast’s six on the road. Kapaun senior safety Preston Hamilton says the win streak is as strong as the bond between his teammates.
“We’re really close this year, which brings out … our record, brings out the way we play. We have each other’s backs, every play. Coach Burrow always says, ‘one more play.’ So, yeah,” Hamilton said.
The bond is also strong among the Golden Eagles, a team facing adversity, but has risen to the occasion. After losing starting quarterback Jonah Mull, John Corrigan has emerged as the team’s new QB-1, a challenge the senior has embraced.
“It’s taken a load off my shoulders being able to wrap at one position before Johnny got hurt. I was repping both quarterback and receiver and just kind of filling in for everybody at that point. And it’s been really great being able to open our passing game up, and these last couple of weeks, just starting the game and just getting to that rhythm,” Corrigan said.
After a 1-2 start, Bishop Carroll roared back with a pair of big city league wins against Wichita Heights and Wichita South. Chris Jaax is building momentum in his first season at the helm. With losses in back-to-back matchups against Kapaun, Bishop Carroll’s message is simple: This is a different team.
“We’ve gotten a lot more physical. He’s really hard on us, and we got a new defensive coordinator too that will help us, and it’s been a really good change,” Bishop Carroll senior defensive end Zach Helton said.
With thousands expected to attend Friday’s game, the kickoff will take place at a bigger venue in Equity Bank Park. Records and rivalries aside, it isn’t just about football between these two schools; it’s about something more.
“There’s a lot of pride that’s going to happen on Friday. The guys know it. They know these guys. Some of them go to church together. Some of them play Little League basketball or baseball. But it’s a big game in this community, and it’s important for bragging rights, no doubt. East side, west side,” Kapaun head football coach Weston Schartz said.
“My kids are in a great school right now, and they’re Catholic grade school resurrection. They’re going to be talking about the game, and they’re going to be excited for the game. And a lot of the kids with grade school are going to go to the game. They don’t go to a lot of the other games, but they’ll go to this game,” Jaax said.
On the field, in the Holy War, two Catholic schools are battling it out, but in the stands, thousands of fans, united through faith.
